title: MemoryQuery and MemoryQueryResult
description: Retrieval against the Memory Service (ADR-0010). Ranking is HYBRID — similarity, recency and importance — not raw cosine, and the weights are surfaced in the result so ranking stays debuggable rather than becoming a black box nobody can tune.

compatibility.notes: `trust_floor` on the result is REQUIRED and is the field most likely to be dropped by someone simplifying this contract. Without it, recalling a memory that originated in a hostile document silently reintroduces that content at the turn's current trust level — laundering through memory. Adding a `kind` value is MAJOR: retention policy keys on kind and an unknown kind has no defined expiry, so it would live forever by accident.

max_trust_level.description: Optional ceiling. Setting `user_originated` excludes memories ingested from external content — useful when the recall will feed a decision that could reach a write tool.

include_redacted.description: Diagnostics only. Redacted records return with cleared text regardless; this only reveals that a tombstone exists.

trust_floor.description: MINIMUM trust across returned records. The caller MUST fold this into the turn's TrustContext.

embedding_model.description: Which model produced the query vector. Recorded so a mid-migration result set is identifiable rather than mysteriously poor (ADR-0013).

degraded.description: True when the Memory Service answered from a partial index or fell back. M5 requires the turn to continue and the user to be told.

examples.query: how do we pick which LLM runs the agent?
